content.overview: Article 110 defines a Money Bill: a Bill is a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with all or any of the matters listed in clause (1) (imposition/abolition/remission/alteration of tax; borrowing; custody of Consolidated/Contingency Funds; appropriation; expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund; receipt/custody/issue of money; incidental matters). A Bill is not a Money Bill by reason only that it provides for imposition of fines or pecuniary penalties, or demands fees for licences/services, or local taxes by local authorities. If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill, the decision of the Speaker of the House of the People is final.
content.glance: Money Bill = only listed money matters (tax, borrowing, funds, appropriation, charged expenditure, etc.). Speaker’s decision final. Fines/fees/local taxes alone do not make it a Money Bill.
content.study:
Article 110(1) lists the exclusive subjects that, alone or in combination, make a Bill a Money Bill (tax; government borrowing; Consolidated Fund / Contingency Fund custody and payment; appropriation of moneys; expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund; receipt, custody, issue or audit of public money; and matters incidental to any of these).

Clause (2): mere provision for fines, licence fees, fees for services, or local authority taxes does not make a Bill a Money Bill.

Clause (3): Speaker’s decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final.

Examination: list the core categories; Speakers’ finality; contrast with ordinary financial Bills under Article 117; link to special procedure in Article 109.

sections.heading: Definitional core
sections.body: A Bill containing only provisions dealing with the listed money matters is a Money Bill. Incidental matters connected with those subjects are included. Fines, licence/service fees, and local taxes alone do not qualify.

sections.heading: Speaker’s certificate
sections.body: If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha thereon is final.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is a Money Bill under Article 110?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 110, a Bill is a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with matters such as imposition or alteration of tax, government borrowing, custody of the Consolidated or Contingency Fund, appropriation of moneys, expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund, and receipt/custody/issue of public money, including incidental matters. Provision only for fines, licence fees, fees for services, or local taxes does not make a Bill a Money Bill. The Speaker’s decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final.

examTips: List money-matter categories; Speaker final; fines/fees alone ≠ Money Bill.
